**Analyzing Grid Patterns**

Okay, I'm zeroing in on the grid structure now. I see the horizontal magenta lines dividing the grid into sections. Each of these sections, defined by the "6s," either contains a pattern or is entirely empty. The objective appears to be completing the blank sections. I've begun to look at sections 0 of example 1, to help get a better understanding of how the sections are arranged.


**Discovering Distance Patterns**

I've made a breakthrough. I realized the patterns within each section represent points at increasing Manhattan distances from the center point (2,2). Section 0 has a single point. Section 1 has four points at distance 1. Section 2 has eight points at distance 2. I'm now testing if Section 3 will contain Manhattan distance 3 points. The sequence of patterns seems to be driven by increasing Manhattan distance. I will focus on this pattern and what it implies for the filled-in sections!


**Confirming Section Logic**

The previous examples confirmed the Manhattan distance pattern, with section 3 containing distance 3 points! I've now examined Example 2, and the key is the movement of pairs of points around the perimeter of the grid. This animation is what defines the sections. The missing sections can be "filled" by continuing the pattern. With Example 3, I confirmed the pattern: each section adds two new points! I have begun to see how the animations drive the generation of the grids.
